info.title: Phantom API
info.description:
Phantom is an OpenAI-compatible API. You buy credit and spend it with a key. Point an OpenAI SDK at `https://phantom.codes/v1`, or an Anthropic SDK at `https://phantom.codes`.

**Paths.** Every route answers on both `/v1/...` and `/api/v1/...`. This reference lists the `/v1` form.

**Keys.** Send `Authorization: Bearer sk-phantom-...`. The `/v1/messages` routes also take `x-api-key`. Phantom keeps only a hash of the key, so a lost key can be recovered only with the recovery code from checkout.

**Money.** Amounts in JSON are US dollars (`_usd` fields). Internally everything is counted in millionths of a dollar, so a dollar figure has at most six decimal places.

**Receipts.** Priced calls return `x-phantom-receipt`, a signed record of what was served. A chat stream sends it as an `event: phantom.receipt` frame ahead of `data: [DONE]`, and a `/v1/messages` stream ahead of `message_stop`.

**Errors.** Inference routes answer in OpenAI's error format, `/v1/messages` in Anthropic's, and the key and purchase routes mostly as `{"error": "..."}`. Each operation lists its statuses.

get.summary: List models for Claude Code
get.description: The models Claude Code lists in its `/model` picker when you set `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://phantom.codes/claude-code` and `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY=1`. Claude Code keeps only ids that contain `claude` or `anthropic`, so each id here starts with `claude-code/`. Phantom drops the prefix again when you send the id as `model`. Lists `phantom-1` first, then current chat models, newest first, leaving out models a newer one from the same maker replaces. Needs no key.

200.description: The models, in the shape of Anthropic's model list. Empty when the upstream could not be reached.

created_at.description: When the upstream published the model, as an ISO 8601 time.

cache-control.description: Caching rules for the response. `public, s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=3600`: the CDN keeps the answer for 5 minutes.

get.summary: List the models Codex can use on Phantom
get.description: The models Codex reads when its provider's `base_url` is `https://phantom.codes/codex/v1`. Codex expects its own list format (`{"models": [...]}`), and without it falls back to generic settings for every model. Each entry carries the model's context window, whether it takes images, and its reasoning levels. Lists `phantom-1` first, then current chat models, newest first, leaving out models a newer one from the same maker replaces. Needs no key.

200.description: The models. Empty when the upstream could not be reached.

models.description: One entry per model, in the format of Codex's `ModelInfo`. Fields not listed here hold the values Codex uses for a model from another provider.

context_window.description: Context window in tokens. Left out when the upstream publishes none.

input_modalities.description: `text`, plus `image` when the model reads images.

cache-control.description: Caching rules for the response. `public, s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=3600`: the CDN keeps the answer for 5 minutes.

post.summary: Create a chat completion from Cursor
post.description: The chat completions API for Cursor. Set Cursor's OpenAI base URL to `https://phantom.codes/cursor/v1`. Cursor can send tool definitions without the `function` wrapper, and Responses-style `input` and `instructions` in place of `messages`. Phantom rewrites those into a standard request, then handles it exactly as `POST /v1/chat/completions`: same auth, billing, headers, receipts and errors. A standard request passes unchanged.

parameters.name: x-phantom-session
parameters.description: Your own conversation id. phantom-1 keeps a conversation's routing state under it: paid chat starts each task on standard and can move it to frontier on any request, tool calls included. Anthropic messages containing only `tool_result` blocks continue the same user message. Other routing (`auto` with a key policy) can keep one model for the session while `stick_minutes` lasts. Only the first 200 characters count. Without this header, Phantom uses Claude Code's `x-claude-code-session-id` when it arrives, and otherwise groups requests by prompt or conversation opening, depending on the route. Phantom stores a salted hash with the selected model and expiry, and keeps provider affinity for the session so its prompt cache stays warm.

parameters.name: x-claude-code-session-id
parameters.description: Claude Code's own session id, which it sends on every request. When `x-phantom-session` is missing, Phantom uses this the same way: the first 200 characters, hashed under the key.

parameters.name: x-claude-code-agent-id
parameters.description: Sent by Claude Code from its helper agents (such as Explore), never from the main agent. phantom-1 runs a helper's request on Standard. Phantom reads only whether the header has a value.

parameters.name: x-openai-subagent
parameters.description: Codex's helper kind. phantom-1 runs `collab_spawn`, `thread_spawn` and `review` on Standard; other kinds, such as `compact`, route as usual.

parameters.name: x-codex-turn-metadata
parameters.description: Codex's turn metadata, as JSON. phantom-1 reads only `subagent_kind`, `thread_source` and `parent_thread_id`, to tell a helper's request apart as with `x-openai-subagent`.

parameters.name: x-codex-parent-thread-id
parameters.description: The Codex thread a helper thread started from. With `thread_source` set to `subagent` in `x-codex-turn-metadata`, it marks a helper's request.

parameters.name: x-phantom-agent
parameters.description: The coding agent a request came through: `claude-code`, `codex`, `cursor`, `gemini-cli` or `coding-agent`. Phantom sets it when you call an agent's base path (`https://phantom.codes/codex/v1`). Any other value is ignored.

parameters.name: x-phantom-route
parameters.description: Send `off` to skip the key's route policy for this request. The request runs on the model it names; `model: "auto"` is refused with a 400.

parameters.name: x-phantom-escalate
parameters.description: Send `1` when the current model isn't managing the task. phantom-1 moves this request one tier up, from standard to frontier. It picks again on the next request, so send the header on each request that should stay up, tool calls included. A key's route policy moves it to the policy's last model. Phantom can't tell a weak answer from a good one, so escalation is your call.

parameters.name: x-phantom-free
parameters.description: Send `off` on a key with no credit to get a `402` instead of having phantom-1 run as `phantom-1:free`, on free models only. A key with credit never runs a free model on phantom-1, so there the header changes nothing.

parameters.name: x-phantom-route-debug
parameters.description: Send `1` or `true` (or set `router_debug: true` in the request body) to get phantom-1's score for each model in `x-phantom-route-scores`. For debugging only; the format may change.

requestBody.description: A chat completions request, in OpenAI's format or Cursor's.

router.description: The router to pick the model: `phantom-1`, `phantom-1:free` or `phantom-1:zdr` (see `GET /v1/routers`). Leave `model` out, or set it to the same router; any other `model` is a 400 `router_model_conflict`. Phantom removes it before calling the upstream.

model.description: A chat model id from `GET /v1/models`; `phantom-1` to let phantom-1 pick its standard or frontier model (a key with no credit runs it as `phantom-1:free`); or `auto` to route by the key's route policy (phantom-1 when the key has none). Renamed ids resolve to the current one. `phantom-1` with an image runs its frontier model. `phantom-1:free` runs only free models, at $0, and needs no credit. `phantom-1:zdr` routes between models with zero data retention on every provider and requires it on every call.

messages.description: The conversation, in OpenAI's format. Needed unless you send `input`.

stream.description: Answer as a server-sent event stream.

stream_options.description: Passed through, with `include_usage` forced to `true` on streams so the usage frame always arrives.

max_tokens.description: Your output limit. Phantom sends the smallest of this, what the balance buys after the prompt, and the model's output cap, shrunk to what the hold covers.

max_completion_tokens.description: Read before `max_tokens` when both are set. When sent, Phantom replaces it with the same limit it sends as `max_tokens`.

n.description: Always sent as 1. One completion per request.

tools.description: Tool definitions. A flat `{name, description, parameters}` is wrapped as `{type: "function", function: {...}}`.

functions.description: Legacy function definitions. Count toward the prompt estimate.

sort.description: How to rank the providers that serve the model before trying them: `cost` (cheapest first, the default), `ttft` (fastest first token) or `tps` (most tokens per second). Overrides the key's route policy. Phantom removes it before calling the upstream.

zdr.description: Only use providers that delete prompts right away (zero data retention). Off by default. Overrides the key's route policy. With it on, phantom-1 skips its free model. Phantom removes it before calling the upstream.

no_training.description: Only use providers that don't train on prompts. Phantom removes it before calling the upstream.

provider.description: The upstream's shorthand for provider routing, such as `{"sort": "tps"}`. `order`, `only` and `sort` pass through, and when it sets `sort`, Phantom sends no default sort. Phantom drops what it sets itself (`caching`, `has`, `models`, `tags`, and a `false` `zeroDataRetention` or `disallowPromptTraining`) and what costs more than the hold (`serviceTier`, `speed`, `sharedRequestType`, `inferenceRegion`, `cache_ttl`).

providerOptions.description: Passed to the upstream, except `gateway.models`, which Phantom replaces with the policy's fallbacks or drops. `gateway.order` still chooses among providers of the same model. Your `gateway` settings win over `sort`. They can't turn off `zdr` or `no_training`. `order` (providers to try first), `only` (the only providers allowed) and `sort` all pass through. Phantom also drops `serviceTier`, `speed` and `sharedRequestType` from `gateway` and from the options of every provider (`openai`, `google`, `vertex`, `xai`, `anthropic`), and a top-level `service_tier` or `speed`, so a call runs at the standard tier. It also drops `inferenceRegion` (a pinned region costs more), `inference_geo`, `cache_ttl` and, on chat, `web_search_options` (a search the hold cannot count), and the `ttl` of any `cache_control` or `cacheControl` (a one-hour cache costs 2x input to write, against the 1.25x Phantom bills), so a call uses the upstream's own region choice and the five-minute cache.

router_debug.description: When true, returns phantom-1's score for each model and the one it picked in `x-phantom-route-scores` header and response body. Phantom removes it before calling the upstream.

input.description: Responses-style input items, turned into `messages` when `messages` is missing. A string counts as one user message.

instructions.description: With `input`: sent as a system message first.

200.description: The upstream's chat completion, passed through. Other statuses from the upstream also come back as the upstream sent them; nothing is billed then.

model.description: The model the upstream reports running. Billing uses this model's rate when the catalog carries it.

choices.description: The completion. One choice, since `n` is forced to 1.

usage.description: What Phantom bills from. When the token counts are missing, Phantom estimates them.

cost.description: What the upstream charged, in US dollars. Billed as-is unless it is more than 100 times the catalog price.

phantom.description: Added by Phantom: what this call cost and how it was served.

cost_usd.description: What this call was charged, in US dollars. Same as `x-phantom-cost-usd`.

provider.description: The provider that answered, or null when the upstream did not say.

attempts.description: Provider attempts across every model tried. 1 when the first try worked.

fallback.description: `true` when a provider or model failed and another one answered.

schema.description: With `stream: true`: the upstream's `data: {chunk}` lines, passed through, ending with `data: [DONE]`. Right before the chunk that holds `data: [DONE]`, Phantom inserts `event: phantom.receipt` with `data: {"receipt":"<compact receipt>","phantom":{...}}`, where `phantom` has the same fields as in a non-streaming answer. That receipt's `output_hash` covers the text you received. Without a signing key the event carries `phantom` only.

x-phantom-request-id.description: Phantom's id for this request (`req_` + 24 hex characters). The same value is `request_id` in the receipt. Also sent when the upstream refuses the call and its error is passed through.

x-phantom-router.description: The router that picked the model: `phantom-1`, `phantom-1:free` or `phantom-1:zdr`. Sent when the request named a router in `router` or `model`, or sent `model: "auto"` on a key with no route policy. The body's `model` names the model that ran. Also sent with a passed-through upstream error. The body adds `router` with the same name, and in a stream the `phantom.receipt` event carries it.

x-phantom-content-logged.description: `false` on every call that reached a model: an answer, or an upstream error passed through. It says Phantom did not store the prompt or the output of this call. A refusal that comes before the call reaches a model (a bad key, a bad body, no credit, a spend cap) does not send it. Also sent with a passed-through upstream error.

x-phantom-routed.description: Present only when the key's route policy picked the model: the model id, then `; reason=` and what decided it. A rule shows as `<condition>:<value>`; other reasons are `default` (the policy's first model), `requested`, `cache` (kept on the conversation's model) and `on_empty` (past the budget, the cheapest model). A `phantom-1` call never sends it; see `x-phantom-route-receipt`. Also sent with a passed-through upstream error.

x-phantom-route-receipt.description: Sent on routed `phantom-1` calls: the model you asked for, the tier and model that ran, how sure phantom-1 was when the pick gives a confidence, and a short reason label. Reason labels may change. Sent on routed phantom-1 calls: names requested model, served tier, underlying model, confidence when the pick gives one, and reason.

x-phantom-route-scores.description: phantom-1's score for each model and the one it picked. Sent only when you ask with `x-phantom-route-debug: 1` or `router_debug: true`. For debugging only; the format may change. Sent when x-phantom-route-debug: 1 or router_debug: true is requested: returns phantom-1's score for each model and the one it picked.

x-phantom-upstream.description: Always `pai`. The receipt's `upstream` field holds the same value. Always `pai`. Also sent with a passed-through upstream error.

x-phantom-upstream-model.description: The model id Phantom sent to the upstream. On chat and messages, the receipt's `model_served` holds the id the upstream reported running. Also sent with a passed-through upstream error.

x-phantom-upstream-request-id.description: The upstream's own request id, copied from its `x-request-id` response header when it sends one. Also sent with a passed-through upstream error.

x-phantom-receipt.description: A signed receipt for the call: `base64url(canonical JSON payload).base64url(signature)`. The payload names the model served, token counts, cost and hashes of the request and response. Check it against `GET /v1/receipts/key`. Left out when the deployment has no signing key. Non-streaming answers only. `model_requested` is the id you sent after renames (`auto` stays `auto`), `model_served` is the `model` field of the upstream's answer, and `reasoning_tokens` comes from `usage.completion_tokens_details`. A stream carries the receipt in the body instead.

x-phantom-cached-tokens.description: Prompt tokens the upstream served from its cache, billed at the cached rate. Non-streaming answers only.

x-phantom-cost-usd.description: What this call was charged, in US dollars. Non-streaming answers only. A stream carries it in the `phantom.receipt` event.

x-phantom-provider.description: The provider that answered, such as `anthropic`, `bedrock` or `azure`. Left out when the upstream does not say. Non-streaming answers only.

x-phantom-fallback.description: `true` when a provider or model failed and another one answered the call, `false` when the first try worked. Non-streaming answers only.

x-phantom-balance-usd.description: Credit left on the key after this call was billed, in US dollars. Left out when the debit found no key to charge; never sent as a guessed zero. Non-streaming answers only. A stream's headers leave before it is billed.

cache-control.description: Caching rules for the response. Streams only: `no-cache`.

400.description: The body is not JSON, `sort`, `zdr` or `no_training` has a bad value (`invalid_prefs`), or the route policy could not route (`route_required`: `auto` with `x-phantom-route: off`, or no model in the policy can take the request). `phantom-1:free` answers `free_model_unfit` when no free model can take the request (images, tools, long context), and `free_needs_key` without an API key. `phantom-1:zdr` answers `zdr_model_unfit` when none of its zero-data-retention models can take the request. With `zdr` on, `zdr_unavailable` means no provider of the model has zero data retention; nothing ran and nothing is billed. A `router` that is not one of `phantom-1`, `phantom-1:free` or `phantom-1:zdr` is `invalid_router`; a `router` with a different `model` is `router_model_conflict`.

401.description: No `Bearer` key (`missing_api_key`; the message says where to buy credit: /checkout, or `POST /v1/purchase/x402` with pay.sh), a key Phantom does not know (`invalid_api_key`), or an expired or deactivated key (`api_key_expired`). A call can't pay for itself with x402 or MPP.

402.description: The key is past its spend cap and its policy did not move the request to its cheapest model (`budget_exceeded`), or it holds less than $0.001, cannot pay for the prompt alone, cannot buy 32 output tokens after it, or the hold failed (`insufficient_quota`).

404.description: The model is not a chat model in the catalog (`model_not_found`), or it was retired (`model_retired`, which names the closest current model).

429.description: The key's per-minute spend cap is reached (`spend_rate_exceeded`). On free models (`phantom-1:free`, and `phantom-1` or `auto` from a key with no credit), counted per workspace: 20 requests a minute (`free_rate_exceeded`) or the daily cap (`free_daily_cap`): 50 a day, 200 a day through a coding agent base path (such as `/codex/v1`), or 1,000 a day once the workspace has taken in $10 of credit. The message says how to raise the cap.

retry-after.description: Seconds to wait before trying again. Sent when the key's per-minute spend cap or a `phantom-1:free` cap is reached: seconds until the minute frees up, or until midnight UTC for the daily cap.

502.description: Phantom has no upstream key configured, or the upstream could not be reached. Nothing is billed.

503.description: The upstream refused Phantom's own account (its credit or budget is used up, or its key is rejected), or Phantom could not load its model list (`upstream_unavailable`). Retry in a few minutes. Nothing is billed.

retry-after.description: Seconds to wait before trying again. Sent when the key's per-minute spend cap or a `phantom-1:free` cap is reached: seconds until the minute frees up, or until midnight UTC for the daily cap.

post.summary: Gemini CLI: generate, stream or count tokens
post.description:
Google's Gemini API, for Gemini CLI. Set `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL=https://phantom.codes/gemini-cli` and `GEMINI_API_KEY` to your Phantom key, and pick a model such as `phantom-1`; `phantom setup` does this for you.

`<model>:generateContent` and `<model>:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse` turn the request into a chat request and handle it exactly as `POST /v1/chat/completions` (same auth, billing, limits and receipts), then answer in Google's format. Gemini CLI's own background calls name bare Google models such as `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`: Phantom runs every bare `gemini-*` name on `phantom-1`, so they work on a key with no credit too. To run a Google model, name it with its maker, as in `google/<model>`.

`<model>:countTokens` answers an estimate (about four characters a token) and needs no key.

Left out on the way: Google's own tools (Search, code execution), `topK`, safety settings and thinking settings. A stream sends text and thinking as they arrive and each tool call whole in the last chunk, with the finish reason and usage; Phantom's `phantom.receipt` event is not sent.

post.summary: Create a chat completion
post.description:
OpenAI's chat completions API, streaming or not. Phantom checks the key, runs its route policy (which picks the model for `model: "auto"`), estimates the prompt from the messages and tool definitions, and holds the worst-case cost on the key. It sets `max_tokens` to the output the hold covers, calls the upstream, and bills the cost the upstream reports in `usage.cost`, or the catalog rate for the reported tokens, at the rate of the model the upstream says it served. Every price includes Phantom's 5% markup on the upstream's rate, the same rates `GET /v1/models` lists. A refused or failed call bills nothing and returns the hold.

A stream bills when it ends: finished, cut off by an error, or abandoned by you. When the usage frame never arrived, the prompt and output tokens fall back to estimates (about four characters per token, tool-call arguments included).

With the policy's `fallback_on_error` on, the upstream tries the policy's other models in the same call when the routed one fails. Phantom always asks the upstream to add prompt-cache markers where a provider needs them (`caching: "auto"`), and tries the cheapest provider of the model first (`sort: "cost"`) unless you set `sort`.

`sort`, `zdr` and `no_training` choose providers; the key's route policy can set them too, and the request wins.

parameters.name: x-phantom-session
parameters.description: Your own conversation id. phantom-1 keeps a conversation's routing state under it: paid chat starts each task on standard and can move it to frontier on any request, tool calls included. Anthropic messages containing only `tool_result` blocks continue the same user message. Other routing (`auto` with a key policy) can keep one model for the session while `stick_minutes` lasts. Only the first 200 characters count. Without this header, Phantom uses Claude Code's `x-claude-code-session-id` when it arrives, and otherwise groups requests by prompt or conversation opening, depending on the route. Phantom stores a salted hash with the selected model and expiry, and keeps provider affinity for the session so its prompt cache stays warm.

parameters.name: x-claude-code-session-id
parameters.description: Claude Code's own session id, which it sends on every request. When `x-phantom-session` is missing, Phantom uses this the same way: the first 200 characters, hashed under the key.

parameters.name: x-claude-code-agent-id
parameters.description: Sent by Claude Code from its helper agents (such as Explore), never from the main agent. phantom-1 runs a helper's request on Standard. Phantom reads only whether the header has a value.

parameters.name: x-openai-subagent
parameters.description: Codex's helper kind. phantom-1 runs `collab_spawn`, `thread_spawn` and `review` on Standard; other kinds, such as `compact`, route as usual.

parameters.name: x-codex-turn-metadata
parameters.description: Codex's turn metadata, as JSON. phantom-1 reads only `subagent_kind`, `thread_source` and `parent_thread_id`, to tell a helper's request apart as with `x-openai-subagent`.

parameters.name: x-codex-parent-thread-id
parameters.description: The Codex thread a helper thread started from. With `thread_source` set to `subagent` in `x-codex-turn-metadata`, it marks a helper's request.

parameters.name: x-phantom-agent
parameters.description: The coding agent a request came through: `claude-code`, `codex`, `cursor`, `gemini-cli` or `coding-agent`. Phantom sets it when you call an agent's base path (`https://phantom.codes/codex/v1`). Any other value is ignored.

parameters.name: x-phantom-route
parameters.description: Send `off` to skip the key's route policy for this request. The request runs on the model it names; `model: "auto"` is refused with a 400.

parameters.name: x-phantom-escalate
parameters.description: Send `1` when the current model isn't managing the task. phantom-1 moves this request one tier up, from standard to frontier. It picks again on the next request, so send the header on each request that should stay up, tool calls included. A key's route policy moves it to the policy's last model. Phantom can't tell a weak answer from a good one, so escalation is your call.

parameters.name: x-phantom-free
parameters.description: Send `off` on a key with no credit to get a `402` instead of having phantom-1 run as `phantom-1:free`, on free models only. A key with credit never runs a free model on phantom-1, so there the header changes nothing.

parameters.name: x-phantom-route-debug
parameters.description: Send `1` or `true` (or set `router_debug: true` in the request body) to get phantom-1's score for each model in `x-phantom-route-scores`. For debugging only; the format may change.

requestBody.description: An OpenAI chat completions request. Fields not listed go to the upstream unchanged.

router.description: The router to pick the model: `phantom-1`, `phantom-1:free` or `phantom-1:zdr` (see `GET /v1/routers`). Leave `model` out, or set it to the same router; any other `model` is a 400 `router_model_conflict`. Phantom removes it before calling the upstream.

model.description: A chat model id from `GET /v1/models`; `phantom-1` to let phantom-1 pick its standard or frontier model (a key with no credit runs it as `phantom-1:free`); or `auto` to route by the key's route policy (phantom-1 when the key has none). Renamed ids resolve to the current one. `phantom-1` with an image runs its frontier model. `phantom-1:free` runs only free models, at $0, and needs no credit. `phantom-1:zdr` routes between models with zero data retention on every provider and requires it on every call.

messages.description: The conversation, in OpenAI's format. Counts toward the prompt estimate, the route policy's conditions, and routing memory. phantom-1 picks a tier for each new user message and keeps it through tool calls; key policies can keep a model by conversation opening.

stream.description: Answer as a server-sent event stream.

stream_options.description: Passed through, with `include_usage` forced to `true` on streams so the usage frame always arrives.

max_tokens.description: Your output limit. Phantom sends the smallest of this, what the balance buys after the prompt, and the model's output cap, shrunk to what the hold covers.

max_completion_tokens.description: Read before `max_tokens` when both are set. When sent, Phantom replaces it with the same limit it sends as `max_tokens`.

n.description: Always sent as 1. One completion per request.

tools.description: Tool definitions. Count toward the prompt estimate. Phantom forwards function and custom tools, `namespace`, `local_shell`, `apply_patch`, a `shell` with `environment.type: "local"`, `tool_search*`, `mcp`, `mcp_toolset`, `bash_*`, `text_editor_*`, `computer_*`, `memory_*`, and the search and fetch tools below. It drops every other tool type without an error, including any it does not know, because a server tool can bill per call. A `web_search*` tool adds the model's price per search, or $0.01 when the upstream lists none, times its `max_uses` to the hold, so a key needs that much more balance. Phantom sets `max_uses` to 5 when you send none and lowers it to 10 when you send more. A `web_fetch*` tool gets `max_uses` the same way and a `max_content_tokens` of at most 20,000, and the hold adds those tokens at the model's input rate. OpenAI's `web_search`, `web_search_preview` and their dated variants have no `max_uses`: on `/v1/responses` Phantom sets `max_tool_calls` to the same count, and on the other routes it drops them. On `phantom-1:free`, and on `phantom-1` from a key with no credit, Phantom drops every `web_search*` tool: each search costs money even on a free model.

functions.description: Legacy function definitions. Count toward the prompt estimate.

sort.description: How to rank the providers that serve the model before trying them: `cost` (cheapest first, the default), `ttft` (fastest first token) or `tps` (most tokens per second). Overrides the key's route policy. Phantom removes it before calling the upstream.

zdr.description: Only use providers that delete prompts right away (zero data retention). Off by default. Overrides the key's route policy. With it on, phantom-1 skips its free model. Phantom removes it before calling the upstream.

no_training.description: Only use providers that don't train on prompts. Phantom removes it before calling the upstream.

provider.description: The upstream's shorthand for provider routing, such as `{"sort": "tps"}`. `order`, `only` and `sort` pass through, and when it sets `sort`, Phantom sends no default sort. Phantom drops what it sets itself (`caching`, `has`, `models`, `tags`, and a `false` `zeroDataRetention` or `disallowPromptTraining`) and what costs more than the hold (`serviceTier`, `speed`, `sharedRequestType`, `inferenceRegion`, `cache_ttl`).

providerOptions.description: Passed to the upstream, except `gateway.models`, which Phantom replaces with the policy's fallbacks or drops. `gateway.order` still chooses among providers of the same model. Phantom also drops `serviceTier`, `speed` and `sharedRequestType` from `gateway` and from the options of every provider (`openai`, `google`, `vertex`, `xai`, `anthropic`), and a top-level `service_tier` or `speed`, so a call runs at the standard tier. post.summary: Test which model a request would be routed to
post.description: Which model a chat request with this body would run on now, and the rule that picked it. Runs the same routing code as `POST /v1/chat/completions` against the key's current budget window and routing memory. Charges nothing and adds nothing to the routing memory. Model selection runs locally without a model call. `phantom-1:free` picks from the free models without calling one, and a spent budget does not stop it.

parameters.name: x-phantom-session
parameters.description: Your own conversation id. phantom-1 keeps a conversation's routing state under it: paid chat starts each task on standard and can move it to frontier on any request, tool calls included. Anthropic messages containing only `tool_result` blocks continue the same user message. Other routing (`auto` with a key policy) can keep one model for the session while `stick_minutes` lasts. Only the first 200 characters count. Without this header, Phantom uses Claude Code's `x-claude-code-session-id` when it arrives, and otherwise groups requests by prompt or conversation opening, depending on the route. Phantom stores a salted hash with the selected model and expiry, and keeps provider affinity for the session so its prompt cache stays warm. Read to find the conversation's remembered model.

parameters.name: x-claude-code-session-id
parameters.description: Claude Code's own session id, which it sends on every request. When `x-phantom-session` is missing, Phantom uses this the same way: the first 200 characters, hashed under the key.

parameters.name: x-claude-code-agent-id
parameters.description: Sent by Claude Code from its helper agents (such as Explore), never from the main agent. phantom-1 runs a helper's request on Standard. Phantom reads only whether the header has a value.

parameters.name: x-openai-subagent
parameters.description: Codex's helper kind. phantom-1 runs `collab_spawn`, `thread_spawn` and `review` on Standard; other kinds, such as `compact`, route as usual.

parameters.name: x-codex-turn-metadata
parameters.description: Codex's turn metadata, as JSON. phantom-1 reads only `subagent_kind`, `thread_source` and `parent_thread_id`, to tell a helper's request apart as with `x-openai-subagent`.

parameters.name: x-codex-parent-thread-id
parameters.description: The Codex thread a helper thread started from. With `thread_source` set to `subagent` in `x-codex-turn-metadata`, it marks a helper's request.

parameters.name: x-phantom-route
parameters.description: Send `off` to skip the key's route policy for this request. The request runs on the model it names; `model: "auto"` is refused with a 400.

parameters.name: x-phantom-escalate
parameters.description: Send `1` when the current model isn't managing the task. phantom-1 moves this request one tier up, from standard to frontier. It picks again on the next request, so send the header on each request that should stay up, tool calls included. A key's route policy moves it to the policy's last model. Phantom can't tell a weak answer from a good one, so escalation is your call. Read the same way the chat route reads it; nothing is remembered.

get.summary: Read the key's spend by model and day
get.description:
What the calling key spent over a date range, by model and by day, and what `phantom-1` routing saved. The range is whole UTC days, `from` and `to` both included, and defaults to this month so far. It covers at most 366 days. Only the calling key shows: to see every key in a workspace, use `GET /v1/workspaces/{id}/spend` with workspace access. Costs are what Phantom charged, markup included. Nothing in the answer carries prompt or completion text, or a key.

`routing` is an estimate. For each call sent to `phantom-1`, `phantom-1:free` or `phantom-1:zdr`, Phantom prices the same tokens on `phantom-1`'s frontier model at that model's price today, and subtracts what the call cost. Calls that already ran on the frontier model count as no saving. A different model may write more or fewer tokens, and prices change, so treat it as a guide. When the frontier model's price isn't listed, `routing.available` is `false` and no figure is given. Calls that asked for `auto` on a key with a route policy aren't counted: the policy, not `phantom-1`, picked their model.

post.summary: Create a message (Anthropic)
post.description:
Anthropic's Messages API on a Phantom key, so Claude Code and the Anthropic SDKs work with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://phantom.codes`. Any chat model in the catalog works, `auto` included. Anthropic ids such as `claude-sonnet-5-5` map to the upstream's `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`.

Billing and routing match `POST /v1/chat/completions`: Phantom runs the key's route policy, estimates the prompt (system prompt, messages and tools), holds the worst-case cost, sets `max_tokens` to what the hold covers, calls the upstream's `/v1/messages`, and bills the cost the upstream reports, or the catalog rate for the reported tokens. Cache reads and cache writes count as input tokens. A refused or failed call bills nothing. A stream bills when it ends, including when you hang up early; output tokens then fall back to an estimate from the text sent so far.

parameters.name: anthropic-version
parameters.description: Anthropic API version, forwarded to the upstream. Defaults to `2023-06-01` when left out.

parameters.name: anthropic-beta
parameters.description: Anthropic beta flags (prompt caching, long context and the like), forwarded to the upstream unchanged.

parameters.name: x-phantom-session
parameters.description: Your own conversation id. phantom-1 keeps a conversation's routing state under it: paid chat starts each task on standard and can move it to frontier on any request, tool calls included. Anthropic messages containing only `tool_result` blocks continue the same user message. Other routing (`auto` with a key policy) can keep one model for the session while `stick_minutes` lasts. Only the first 200 characters count. Without this header, Phantom uses Claude Code's `x-claude-code-session-id` when it arrives, and otherwise groups requests by prompt or conversation opening, depending on the route. Phantom stores a salted hash with the selected model and expiry, and keeps provider affinity for the session so its prompt cache stays warm.

parameters.name: x-claude-code-session-id
parameters.description: Claude Code's own session id, which it sends on every request. When `x-phantom-session` is missing, Phantom uses this the same way: the first 200 characters, hashed under the key.

parameters.name: x-claude-code-agent-id
parameters.description: Sent by Claude Code from its helper agents (such as Explore), never from the main agent. phantom-1 runs a helper's request on Standard. Phantom reads only whether the header has a value.

parameters.name: x-openai-subagent
parameters.description: Codex's helper kind. phantom-1 runs `collab_spawn`, `thread_spawn` and `review` on Standard; other kinds, such as `compact`, route as usual.

parameters.name: x-codex-turn-metadata
parameters.description: Codex's turn metadata, as JSON. phantom-1 reads only `subagent_kind`, `thread_source` and `parent_thread_id`, to tell a helper's request apart as with `x-openai-subagent`.

parameters.name: x-codex-parent-thread-id
parameters.description: The Codex thread a helper thread started from. With `thread_source` set to `subagent` in `x-codex-turn-metadata`, it marks a helper's request.

parameters.name: x-phantom-agent
parameters.description: The coding agent a request came through: `claude-code`, `codex`, `cursor`, `gemini-cli` or `coding-agent`. Phantom sets it when you call an agent's base path (`https://phantom.codes/codex/v1`). Any other value is ignored.

parameters.name: x-phantom-route
parameters.description: Send `off` to skip the key's route policy for this request. The request runs on the model it names; `model: "auto"` is refused with a 400.

parameters.name: x-phantom-escalate
parameters.description: Send `1` when the current model isn't managing the task. phantom-1 moves this request one tier up, from standard to frontier. It picks again on the next request, so send the header on each request that should stay up, tool calls included. A key's route policy moves it to the policy's last model. Phantom can't tell a weak answer from a good one, so escalation is your call.

parameters.name: x-phantom-free
parameters.description: Send `off` on a key with no credit to get a `402` instead of having phantom-1 run as `phantom-1:free`, on free models only. A key with credit never runs a free model on phantom-1, so there the header changes nothing.

requestBody.description: An Anthropic Messages request. Fields not listed go to the upstream unchanged.

router.description: The router to pick the model: `phantom-1`, `phantom-1:free` or `phantom-1:zdr` (see `GET /v1/routers`). Leave `model` out, or set it to the same router; any other `model` is a 400 `router_model_conflict`. Phantom removes it before calling the upstream.

model.description: Required unless the request sends `router`. A chat model id, an Anthropic `claude-*` id, `phantom-1` to let phantom-1 pick, or `auto` to route by the key's route policy (phantom-1 when the key has none). `phantom-1:free` runs only free models, at $0, and needs no credit. `phantom-1:zdr` routes between models with zero data retention on every provider and requires it on every call.

messages.description: The conversation, in Anthropic's format. Must be non-empty.

max_tokens.description: Your output limit. Phantom replaces it with the smallest of this, what the balance buys, and the model's output cap, then shrinks it to what the hold covers.

stream.description: Answer as a server-sent event stream.

system.description: The system prompt. Anthropic also accepts an array of text blocks. Counts toward the prompt estimate.

tools.description: Tool definitions. Count toward the prompt estimate and the route policy's conditions. Phantom forwards function and custom tools, `namespace`, `local_shell`, `apply_patch`, a `shell` with `environment.type: "local"`, `tool_search*`, `mcp`, `mcp_toolset`, `bash_*`, `text_editor_*`, `computer_*`, `memory_*`, and the search and fetch tools below. It drops every other tool type without an error, including any it does not know, because a server tool can bill per call. A `web_search*` tool adds the model's price per search, or $0.01 when the upstream lists none, times its `max_uses` to the hold, so a key needs that much more balance. Phantom sets `max_uses` to 5 when you send none and lowers it to 10 when you send more. A `web_fetch*` tool gets `max_uses` the same way and a `max_content_tokens` of at most 20,000, and the hold adds those tokens at the model's input rate. OpenAI's `web_search`, `web_search_preview` and their dated variants have no `max_uses`: on `/v1/responses` Phantom sets `max_tool_calls` to the same count, and on the other routes it drops them. On `phantom-1:free`, and on `phantom-1` from a key with no credit, Phantom drops every `web_search*` tool: each search costs money even on a free model.

thinking.description: Extended thinking. When `max_tokens` is lowered below `budget_tokens`, the budget drops to `max_tokens - 1`; when that is under 1024, thinking is removed from the request. `type: "enabled"` also counts as reasoning for the route policy.

budget_tokens.description: Most tokens the model may spend thinking.

models.description: Dropped. Phantom never lets the upstream pick a model it did not price.

sort.description: How to rank the providers that serve the model: `cost` (the default), `ttft` (fastest first token) or `tps` (most tokens per second). Overrides the key's route policy. Removed before calling the upstream.

zdr.description: Only use providers that delete prompts right away. Off by default. Overrides the key's route policy. With it on, phantom-1 skips its free model. Removed before calling the upstream.

no_training.description: Only use providers that don't train on prompts. Removed before calling the upstream.

providerOptions.description: Passed to the upstream, except `gateway.models`, which is dropped. `gateway.order` still chooses among providers of the same model. Phantom always sets `gateway.caching: "auto"`, and `gateway.sort: "cost"` unless you choose a sort. Your `gateway` settings win over `sort`. They can't turn off `zdr` or `no_training`. Phantom also drops `serviceTier`, `speed` and `sharedRequestType` from `gateway` and from the options of every provider (`openai`, `google`, `vertex`, `xai`, `anthropic`), and a top-level `service_tier` or `speed`, so a call runs at the standard tier. It also drops `inferenceRegion` (a pinned region costs more), `inference_geo` and `cache_ttl`, and the `ttl` of any `cache_control` or `cacheControl` (a one-hour cache costs 2x input to write, against the 1.25x Phantom bills), so a call uses the upstream's own region choice and the five-minute cache.

200.description: The upstream's Anthropic message, passed through. Other statuses from the upstream also come back as the upstream sent them, with its Anthropic error body; nothing is billed then.

model.description: The model the upstream reports running. Billing uses this model's rate when the catalog carries it.

content.description: The output blocks: text, thinking, tool use.

usage.description: Token counts Phantom bills from. When they are missing, Phantom estimates from the prompt and the content.

cache_read_input_tokens.description: Input tokens read from the cache.

cache_creation_input_tokens.description: Input tokens written to the cache.

phantom.description: Added by Phantom: what this call cost and how it was served.

cost_usd.description: What this call was charged, in US dollars.

provider.description: The provider that answered, or null when the upstream did not say.

attempts.description: Provider attempts across every model tried. 1 when the first try worked.

fallback.description: `true` when a provider or model failed and another one answered.

schema.description: With `stream: true`: the upstream's Anthropic events (`message_start`, `content_block_delta`, `message_delta`, `message_stop` and the rest), passed through. Right before the chunk that holds `event: message_stop`, Phantom inserts `event: phantom.receipt` with `data: {"type":"phantom.receipt","receipt":"<compact receipt>","phantom":{...}}`, where `phantom` has the same fields as in a non-streaming answer. Without a signing key the event carries `phantom` only.

x-phantom-request-id.description: Phantom's id for this request (`req_` + 24 hex characters). The same value is `request_id` in the receipt. Also sent when the upstream refuses the call and its error is passed through.

x-phantom-router.description: The router that picked the model: `phantom-1`, `phantom-1:free` or `phantom-1:zdr`. Sent when the request named a router in `router` or `model`, or sent `model: "auto"` on a key with no route policy. The body's `model` names the model that ran. Also sent with a passed-through upstream error. The body adds `router` with the same name, and in a stream the `phantom.receipt` event carries it.

x-phantom-content-logged.description: `false` on every call that reached a model: an answer, or an upstream error passed through. It says Phantom did not store the prompt or the output of this call. A refusal that comes before the call reaches a model (a bad key, a bad body, no credit, a spend cap) does not send it. Also sent with a passed-through upstream error.

x-phantom-routed.description: Present only when the key's route policy picked the model: the model id, then `; reason=` and what decided it. A rule shows as `<condition>:<value>`; other reasons are `default` (the policy's first model), `requested`, `cache` (kept on the conversation's model) and `on_empty` (past the budget, the cheapest model). A `phantom-1` call never sends it; see `x-phantom-route-receipt`. Also sent with a passed-through upstream error.

x-phantom-route-receipt.description: Sent on routed `phantom-1` calls: the model you asked for, the tier and model that ran, how sure phantom-1 was when the pick gives a confidence, and a short reason label. Reason labels may change. Sent on routed phantom-1 calls: names requested model, served tier, underlying model, confidence when the pick gives one, and reason.

x-phantom-route-scores.description: phantom-1's score for each model and the one it picked. Sent only when you ask with `x-phantom-route-debug: 1` or `router_debug: true`. For debugging only; the format may change. Sent when debug mode is requested: returns phantom-1's score for each model and the one it picked.

x-phantom-upstream.description: Always `pai`. The receipt's `upstream` field holds the same value. Always `pai`. Also sent with a passed-through upstream error.

x-phantom-upstream-model.description: The model id Phantom sent to the upstream. On chat and messages, the receipt's `model_served` holds the id the upstream reported running. Also sent with a passed-through upstream error.

x-phantom-upstream-request-id.description: The upstream's own request id, copied from its `x-request-id` response header when it sends one. Also sent with a passed-through upstream error.

x-phantom-receipt.description: A signed receipt for the call: `base64url(canonical JSON payload).base64url(signature)`. The payload names the model served, token counts, cost and hashes of the request and response. Check it against `GET /v1/receipts/key`. Left out when the deployment has no signing key. Non-streaming answers only. `model_requested` is the id you sent after renames (`auto` stays `auto`), `model_served` is the `model` field of the upstream's answer, and `reasoning_tokens` is 0. A stream carries the receipt in the body instead.

x-phantom-cached-tokens.description: Prompt tokens the upstream served from its cache, billed at the cached rate. Non-streaming answers only: the `cache_read_input_tokens` the upstream reported.

x-phantom-cost-usd.description: What this call was charged, in US dollars. Non-streaming answers only. A stream carries it in the `phantom.receipt` event.

x-phantom-provider.description: The provider that answered, such as `anthropic`, `bedrock` or `azure`. Left out when the upstream does not say. Non-streaming answers only.

x-phantom-fallback.description: `true` when a provider or model failed and another one answered the call, `false` when the first try worked. Non-streaming answers only.

x-phantom-balance-usd.description: Credit left on the key after this call was billed, in US dollars. Left out when the debit found no key to charge; never sent as a guessed zero. Non-streaming answers only. A stream's headers leave before it is billed.

cache-control.description: Caching rules for the response. Streams only: `no-cache`.

400.description: The body is not JSON, `model` or `messages` is missing, `sort`, `zdr` or `no_training` has a bad value, or the route policy could not route (for example `auto` with `x-phantom-route: off`, or no model in the policy can take the request). `phantom-1:free` answers 400 when no free model can take the request (images, tools, long context), and without an API key. `phantom-1:zdr` answers `zdr_model_unfit` when none of its zero-data-retention models can take the request. With `zdr` on, `zdr_unavailable` means no provider of the model has zero data retention; nothing ran and nothing is billed. A `router` that is not one of `phantom-1`, `phantom-1:free` or `phantom-1:zdr` is `invalid_router`; a `router` with a different `model` is `router_model_conflict`.

401.description: No key in `x-api-key` or `Authorization` (the message says where to buy credit: /checkout, or `POST /v1/purchase/x402` with pay.sh), a key Phantom does not know, or an expired or deactivated key. A call can't pay for itself with x402 or MPP.

402.description: The key is past its spend cap (and its policy did not move the request to its cheapest model), holds less than $0.001, cannot pay for the prompt alone, cannot buy 32 output tokens after it, or the hold failed.

404.description: The model is not a chat model in the catalog, or it was retired (the error names the closest current model).

429.description: The key's per-minute spend cap is reached. On free models (`phantom-1:free`, and `phantom-1` or `auto` from a key with no credit), counted per workspace: 20 requests a minute (`free_rate_exceeded`) or the daily cap (`free_daily_cap`): 50 a day, 200 a day through a coding agent base path (such as `/codex/v1`), or 1,000 a day once the workspace has taken in $10 of credit. The message says how to raise the cap.

retry-after.description: Seconds to wait before trying again. Sent when the key's per-minute spend cap or a `phantom-1:free` cap is reached: seconds until the minute frees up, or until midnight UTC for the daily cap.

502.description: Phantom has no upstream key configured, or the upstream could not be reached. Nothing is billed.

503.description: The upstream refused Phantom's own account (its credit or budget is used up, or its key is rejected), or Phantom could not load its model list (`upstream_unavailable`). Retry in a few minutes. Nothing is billed.

retry-after.description: Seconds to wait before trying again. Sent when the key's per-minute spend cap or a `phantom-1:free` cap is reached: seconds until the minute frees up, or until midnight UTC for the daily cap.

The PaymentIntent allows only payment methods that never redirect the buyer (cards, Link and wallets), and a card that needs 3D Secure completes it in Stripe's dialog, so the buyer stays on the page. Then poll `GET /v1/purchase/{id}/status`. The card is charged the price plus Stripe's card fee (see `card_fee_bps` in `GET /v1/bundles`). From $50 Phantom pays Stripe's fixed 30 cents, so the card pays only the percentage. The key receives the price, plus bonus credit from $100 (`bonus_tiers` in `GET /v1/bundles`); `credit_usd` says how much. Needs no key. Keep `recovery_code`: it is shown once, and it is the only way to get the key back if the page is lost.

get.summary: Poll a purchase and collect its key once paid
get.description:
Reports where a purchase stands and, once it is paid, hands back the key. For a Solana payment each poll also looks for the transfer on chain (at most every few seconds per server). When a finalized transfer has landed with the reference, exactly the owed amount (Stripe books only an exact amount, so more or less is not counted) and a time inside the quote window plus a short grace, the poll records it with Stripe. The payment stays `pending` until Stripe's signed webhook marks it paid, usually within a minute. A buyer who closes the page early is not stuck: the daily cleanup job and `POST /v1/purchase/recover` look for the transfer too. A card or Stripe crypto payment is marked paid by Stripe's webhook.

A paid purchase that named a key credits that key's workspace and extends the key's expiry to at least the new validity; no key comes back. If the key was rotated or revoked before Stripe confirmed the payment, the credit still lands in its workspace, where the replacement key spends it. Otherwise the new key is sealed with the recovery code, so send `x-phantom-recovery-code` to get it. The first poll with the code creates the key; later polls with the code return the same key. Needs no API key. This route is left out of the purchase rate limit.

Scores each document against a query. Phantom estimates the input from the query and the documents (about four characters per token), holds that cost on the key, and sends the request to the upstream's rerank endpoint. It bills the `usage.cost` the upstream reports when there is one, otherwise the estimate. A failed call bills nothing and returns the hold.

When the upstream refuses the request with a 4xx status, that status comes back unchanged in an OpenAI error with code `upstream_unavailable`.

post.summary: Create a response (Responses API)
post.description:
OpenAI's Responses API, streaming or not, so Codex CLI and the OpenAI SDK's `responses.create` work on a Phantom key. Any chat model in the catalog works, `auto` included.

Billing and routing match `POST /v1/chat/completions`: Phantom runs the key's route policy, estimates the prompt (instructions, input and tools), holds the worst-case cost, sets `max_output_tokens` to what the hold covers, calls the upstream's `/v1/responses`, and bills the cost the upstream reports, or the catalog rate for the reported tokens. A refused or failed call bills nothing. A stream bills when it ends, including when you hang up early.

Phantom keeps no conversation: `store` is always sent as `false`, and `previous_response_id` is refused. Send the whole conversation in `input`, as Codex does.

parameters.name: x-phantom-session
parameters.description: Your own conversation id. phantom-1 keeps a conversation's routing state under it: paid chat starts each task on standard and can move it to frontier on any request, tool calls included. Anthropic messages containing only `tool_result` blocks continue the same user message. Other routing (`auto` with a key policy) can keep one model for the session while `stick_minutes` lasts. Only the first 200 characters count. Without this header, Phantom uses Claude Code's `x-claude-code-session-id` when it arrives, and otherwise groups requests by prompt or conversation opening, depending on the route. Phantom stores a salted hash with the selected model and expiry, and keeps provider affinity for the session so its prompt cache stays warm.

parameters.name: x-claude-code-session-id
parameters.description: Claude Code's own session id, which it sends on every request. When `x-phantom-session` is missing, Phantom uses this the same way: the first 200 characters, hashed under the key.

parameters.name: x-claude-code-agent-id
parameters.description: Sent by Claude Code from its helper agents (such as Explore), never from the main agent. phantom-1 runs a helper's request on Standard. Phantom reads only whether the header has a value.

parameters.name: x-openai-subagent
parameters.description: Codex's helper kind. phantom-1 runs `collab_spawn`, `thread_spawn` and `review` on Standard; other kinds, such as `compact`, route as usual.

parameters.name: x-codex-turn-metadata
parameters.description: Codex's turn metadata, as JSON. phantom-1 reads only `subagent_kind`, `thread_source` and `parent_thread_id`, to tell a helper's request apart as with `x-openai-subagent`.

parameters.name: x-codex-parent-thread-id
parameters.description: The Codex thread a helper thread started from. With `thread_source` set to `subagent` in `x-codex-turn-metadata`, it marks a helper's request.

parameters.name: x-phantom-agent
parameters.description: The coding agent a request came through: `claude-code`, `codex`, `cursor`, `gemini-cli` or `coding-agent`. Phantom sets it when you call an agent's base path (`https://phantom.codes/codex/v1`). Any other value is ignored.

parameters.name: x-phantom-route
parameters.description: Send `off` to skip the key's route policy for this request. The request runs on the model it names; `model: "auto"` is refused with a 400.

parameters.name: x-phantom-escalate
parameters.description: Send `1` when the current model isn't managing the task. phantom-1 moves this request one tier up, from standard to frontier. It picks again on the next request, so send the header on each request that should stay up, tool calls included. A key's route policy moves it to the policy's last model. Phantom can't tell a weak answer from a good one, so escalation is your call.

parameters.name: x-phantom-free
parameters.description: Send `off` on a key with no credit to get a `402` instead of having phantom-1 run as `phantom-1:free`, on free models only. A key with credit never runs a free model on phantom-1, so there the header changes nothing.

requestBody.description: A Responses API request. Fields not listed go to the upstream unchanged.

router.description: The router to pick the model: `phantom-1`, `phantom-1:free` or `phantom-1:zdr` (see `GET /v1/routers`). Leave `model` out, or set it to the same router; any other `model` is a 400 `router_model_conflict`. Phantom removes it before calling the upstream.

model.description: A chat model id from `GET /v1/models`; `phantom-1` to let phantom-1 pick its standard or frontier model (a key with no credit runs it as `phantom-1:free`); or `auto` to route by the key's route policy (phantom-1 when the key has none). `phantom-1` with an image runs its frontier model. `phantom-1:free` runs only free models, at $0, and needs no credit. `phantom-1:zdr` routes between models with zero data retention on every provider and requires it on every call.

input.description: The prompt, or an array of input items (messages, function call outputs). Counts toward the prompt estimate.

instructions.description: The system prompt. Counts toward the prompt estimate.

tools.description: Tool definitions. Count toward the prompt estimate. Phantom forwards function and custom tools, `namespace`, `local_shell`, `apply_patch`, a `shell` with `environment.type: "local"`, `tool_search*`, `mcp`, `mcp_toolset`, `bash_*`, `text_editor_*`, `computer_*`, `memory_*`, and the search and fetch tools below. It drops every other tool type without an error, including any it does not know, because a server tool can bill per call. A `web_search*` tool adds the model's price per search, or $0.01 when the upstream lists none, times its `max_uses` to the hold, so a key needs that much more balance. Phantom sets `max_uses` to 5 when you send none and lowers it to 10 when you send more. A `web_fetch*` tool gets `max_uses` the same way and a `max_content_tokens` of at most 20,000, and the hold adds those tokens at the model's input rate. OpenAI's `web_search`, `web_search_preview` and their dated variants have no `max_uses`: on `/v1/responses` Phantom sets `max_tool_calls` to the same count, and on the other routes it drops them. On `phantom-1:free`, and on `phantom-1` from a key with no credit, Phantom drops every `web_search*` tool: each search costs money even on a free model.

stream.description: Answer as a server-sent event stream.

max_output_tokens.description: Your output limit. Phantom replaces it with the smallest of this, what the balance buys, and the model's output cap, then shrinks it to what the hold covers.

store.description: Always sent as `false`. Phantom keeps no conversation.

previous_response_id.description: Refused with 400. Send the whole conversation in `input`.

sort.description: How to rank the providers that serve the model: `cost` (the default), `ttft` (fastest first token) or `tps` (most tokens per second). Removed before calling the upstream.

zdr.description: Only use providers that delete prompts right away. Off by default. Overrides the key's route policy. With it on, phantom-1 skips its free model. Removed before calling the upstream.

no_training.description: Only use providers that don't train on prompts. Removed before calling the upstream.

providerOptions.description: Passed to the upstream, except `gateway.models`, which is dropped. Phantom always sets `gateway.caching: "auto"`, and `gateway.sort: "cost"` unless you choose a sort. Phantom also drops `serviceTier`, `speed` and `sharedRequestType` from `gateway` and from the options of every provider (`openai`, `google`, `vertex`, `xai`, `anthropic`), and a top-level `service_tier` or `speed`, so a call runs at the standard tier. It also drops `inferenceRegion` (a pinned region costs more), `inference_geo` and `cache_ttl`, and the `ttl` of any `cache_control` or `cacheControl` (a one-hour cache costs 2x input to write, against the 1.25x Phantom bills), so a call uses the upstream's own region choice and the five-minute cache.

200.description: The upstream's response, passed through, plus `phantom`. Other statuses from the upstream also come back as the upstream sent them; nothing is billed then.

model.description: The model the upstream reports running.

output.description: Output items: messages, reasoning, function calls.

usage.description: Token counts Phantom bills from. When they are missing, Phantom estimates them.

phantom.description: Added by Phantom: what this call cost and how it was served.

cost_usd.description: What this call was charged, in US dollars.

provider.description: The provider that answered, or null when the upstream did not say.

attempts.description: Provider attempts across every model tried.

fallback.description: `true` when a provider or model failed and another one answered.

schema.description: With `stream: true`: the upstream's Responses events, passed through. Right before the chunk that holds the terminal event (`response.completed`, `response.incomplete` or `response.failed`), Phantom inserts `event: phantom.receipt` with `data: {"type":"phantom.receipt","receipt":"<compact receipt>","phantom":{...}}`. Without a signing key the event carries `phantom` only. Clients that don't know the event ignore it.

x-phantom-request-id.description: Phantom's id for this request (`req_` + 24 hex characters). The same value is `request_id` in the receipt. Also sent with a passed-through upstream error.

x-phantom-router.description: The router that picked the model: `phantom-1`, `phantom-1:free` or `phantom-1:zdr`. Sent when the request named a router in `router` or `model`, or sent `model: "auto"` on a key with no route policy. The body's `model` names the model that ran. Also sent with a passed-through upstream error. The body adds `router` with the same name, and in a stream the `phantom.receipt` event carries it.

x-phantom-content-logged.description: `false` on every call that reached a model: an answer, or an upstream error passed through. It says Phantom did not store the prompt or the output of this call. A refusal that comes before the call reaches a model (a bad key, a bad body, no credit, a spend cap) does not send it. Also sent with a passed-through upstream error.

x-phantom-routed.description: Present only when the key's route policy picked the model: the model id, then `; reason=` and what decided it. A rule shows as `<condition>:<value>`; other reasons are `default` (the policy's first model), `requested`, `cache` (kept on the conversation's model) and `on_empty` (past the budget, the cheapest model). A `phantom-1` call never sends it; see `x-phantom-route-receipt`. Also sent with a passed-through upstream error.

x-phantom-route-receipt.description: Sent on routed `phantom-1` calls: the model you asked for, the tier and model that ran, how sure phantom-1 was when the pick gives a confidence, and a short reason label. Reason labels may change. Sent on routed phantom-1 calls: names requested model, served tier, underlying model, confidence when the pick gives one, and reason.

x-phantom-route-scores.description: phantom-1's score for each model and the one it picked. Sent only when you ask with `x-phantom-route-debug: 1` or `router_debug: true`. For debugging only; the format may change. Sent when debug mode is requested: returns phantom-1's score for each model and the one it picked.

x-phantom-upstream.description: Always `pai`. The receipt's `upstream` field holds the same value. Always `pai`. Also sent with a passed-through upstream error.

x-phantom-upstream-model.description: The model id Phantom sent to the upstream. On chat and messages, the receipt's `model_served` holds the id the upstream reported running. Also sent with a passed-through upstream error.

x-phantom-upstream-request-id.description: The upstream's own request id, copied from its `x-request-id` response header when it sends one. Also sent with a passed-through upstream error.

x-phantom-receipt.description: A signed receipt for the call: `base64url(canonical JSON payload).base64url(signature)`. The payload names the model served, token counts, cost and hashes of the request and response. Check it against `GET /v1/receipts/key`. Left out when the deployment has no signing key. Non-streaming answers only. A stream carries the receipt in the body instead.

x-phantom-cached-tokens.description: Prompt tokens the upstream served from its cache, billed at the cached rate. Non-streaming answers only: `usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens`.

x-phantom-cost-usd.description: What this call was charged, in US dollars. Non-streaming answers only. A stream carries it in the `phantom.receipt` event.

x-phantom-provider.description: The provider that answered, such as `anthropic`, `bedrock` or `azure`. Left out when the upstream does not say. Non-streaming answers only.

x-phantom-fallback.description: `true` when a provider or model failed and another one answered the call, `false` when the first try worked. Non-streaming answers only.

x-phantom-balance-usd.description: Credit left on the key after this call was billed, in US dollars. Left out when the debit found no key to charge; never sent as a guessed zero. Non-streaming answers only.

cache-control.description: Caching rules for the response. Streams only: `no-cache`.

400.description: The body is not JSON, `input` is missing, `previous_response_id` is set, `sort`, `zdr` or `no_training` has a bad value, or the route policy could not route. `phantom-1:free` answers `free_model_unfit` when no free model can take the request (images, tools, long context), and `free_needs_key` without an API key. `phantom-1:zdr` answers `zdr_model_unfit` when none of its zero-data-retention models can take the request. With `zdr` on, `zdr_unavailable` means no provider of the model has zero data retention; nothing ran and nothing is billed. A `router` that is not one of `phantom-1`, `phantom-1:free` or `phantom-1:zdr` is `invalid_router`; a `router` with a different `model` is `router_model_conflict`.

401.description: No `Bearer` key (the message says where to buy credit: /checkout, or `POST /v1/purchase/x402` with pay.sh), a key Phantom does not know, or an expired or deactivated key. A call can't pay for itself with x402 or MPP.

402.description: The key is past its spend cap, cannot pay for the prompt, cannot buy 32 output tokens after it, or the hold failed.

404.description: The model is not a chat model in the catalog, or it was retired.

429.description: The key's per-minute spend cap is reached. On free models (`phantom-1:free`, and `phantom-1` or `auto` from a key with no credit), counted per workspace: 20 requests a minute (`free_rate_exceeded`) or the daily cap (`free_daily_cap`): 50 a day, 200 a day through a coding agent base path (such as `/codex/v1`), or 1,000 a day once the workspace has taken in $10 of credit. The message says how to raise the cap.

retry-after.description: Seconds to wait before trying again. Sent when the key's per-minute spend cap or a `phantom-1:free` cap is reached: seconds until the minute frees up, or until midnight UTC for the daily cap.

502.description: Phantom has no upstream key configured, or the upstream could not be reached. Nothing is billed.

503.description: The upstream refused Phantom's own account (its credit or budget is used up, or its key is rejected), or Phantom could not load its model list (`upstream_unavailable`). Retry in a few minutes. Nothing is billed.

retry-after.description: Seconds to wait before trying again. Sent when the key's per-minute spend cap or a `phantom-1:free` cap is reached: seconds until the minute frees up, or until midnight UTC for the daily cap.

A job that later fails is refunded by the poll. If the job starts but Phantom cannot save it, the charge is refunded here and the answer is `502`.

duration.description: Same as `seconds`, read only when `seconds` is absent.

resolution.description: Saved with the job and nothing more. It is not sent upstream and does not change the price.

size.description: Same as `resolution`, read only when `resolution` is absent.

get.summary: Poll a video generation job for its result
get.description:
Reports a video job started with `POST /v1/video/generations`. Phantom looks the job up by its id and the calling key together, so another key cannot read it. A finished or failed job is answered from Phantom's record without asking the upstream again. A running job is checked with the upstream on each poll.

When the upstream reports an error, or reports the job done with no video, Phantom marks the job failed and refunds the charge. Only the poll that marks it failed refunds, so a charge is never refunded twice. If the refund does not go through, the job goes back to running and the poll answers `502 refund_failed`; poll again.

A finished job carries the upstream's video URL. Phantom does not copy the file.

Sent with a `completed` answer only. On this route `model_served` is the job's model id, the token counts are 0, `upstream_request_id` is `null`, and `input_hash` covers the job settings (model, seconds, resolution, audio) rather than the prompt, which Phantom does not keep.

get.summary: Read the workspace's spend by key, model and day
get.description:
What every key in the workspace spent over a date range, by key name, model and day, and what `phantom-1` routing saved. Needs workspace ownership or a management credential; an inference key gets 401, and one key reads only its own spend at `GET /v1/key/spend`. The range is whole UTC days, `from` and `to` both included, and defaults to this month so far. It covers at most 366 days. Keys are named, never listed by hash, and a key that was revoked or rotated away stays in the list with `active: false` so its history keeps its name. Costs are what Phantom charged, markup included. Nothing in the answer carries prompt or completion text, or a key.

`routing` is an estimate. For each call sent to `phantom-1`, `phantom-1:free` or `phantom-1:zdr`, Phantom prices the same tokens on `phantom-1`'s frontier model at that model's price today, and subtracts what the call cost. Calls that already ran on the frontier model count as no saving. A different model may write more or fewer tokens, and prices change, so treat it as a guide. When the frontier model's price isn't listed, `routing.available` is `false` and no figure is given. Calls that asked for `auto` on a key with a route policy aren't counted: the policy, not `phantom-1`, picked their model.
